name: ChatThread
description: Mortar chat thread: a scrollable log of a live conversation with author avatars, names, roles and times, own messages aligned to the end, a Markdown body slot, a streaming responding state, inline errors with retry and quick-answer choices; it stays pinned to the newest message unless the reader scrolls up.

props.label: string (accessible name of the conversation log)
props.messages: { id: string; author: { name: string; role?: string; image?: string }; content?: ReactNode; own?: boolean; time?: string; dateTime?: string; status?: "complete" | "streaming" | "error"; error?: string; onRetry?: () => void }[]
props.choices: string[] (quick answers under the latest message from someone else)
props.empty: { title: string; description?: string; action?: ReactNode }

contract.usage: Import { ChatThread } from @tonycodes-ui/mortar. Place it in a flex column with a fixed height (for example above a ChatComposer) so it can scroll. Pass rendered Markdown as each message's content and mark a reply that is still arriving with status "streaming".
contract.avoid: Do not use it for static marketing mock-ups (use ChatPreview) or comment threads without live replies (use ActivityFeed). Do not copy implementations or override central colours.
contract.accessibility: The scroll area is a focusable role="log" named by label. While a reply streams the log is aria-busy, so screen readers announce the reply once it is complete instead of every token. Avatars are decorative; the author's name and role are text. Quick answers are a named group of buttons.
